contract: Prompt 193, validation contract for the Galilean-moon kernel, committed before any candidate output was inspected (the pack's own held-out errors, in ephemeris-packs/galilean-2025-11.json, and the moons' largest elongations, 5.9, 9.5, 15.0 and 26.5 Jupiter radii, were seen first and fix nothing below).

observatory.name: Kitt Peak, Arizona (a stated example site)

a1.packVsHorizons.claim: the pack reproduces Horizons at the half-hour samples it never saw
a1.packVsHorizons.bound: each moon's held-out position error at most 5 km and velocity error at most 1e-3 km/s

a2.geometryVsOracle.claim: the kernel's offsets of each moon from Jupiter (x, y in Jupiter radii) agree with an independent numpy and astropy computation from the raw hourly Horizons rows (cubic Hermite) and astropy's built-in Jupiter
a2.geometryVsOracle.bound: largest difference over 48 epochs at most 0.002 Jupiter radii in x and in y

b1.aliasNightly.claim: once-nightly sampling cannot tell Io's period from its alias
b1.aliasNightly.bound: from the truth marks sampled at the nightly points only (exactly one day apart), the fit at Io's alias period (2.3 d) and at its true period differ in chi-square by less than 1 (noise 0.03 Jupiter radii); Europa, Ganymede and Callisto have no alias below the Nyquist period of 2 days

b2.aliasDesigned.claim: the designed cadence tells them apart
b2.aliasDesigned.bound: from the truth marks at the designed epochs, the best period for every moon beats any alias candidate by a chi-square difference of at least 100, and is the one within 0.3 percent of the reference sidereal period

c1.periodAmplitude.claim: a sinusoid fitted to the truth marks recovers each moon's period and semi-major axis
c1.periodAmplitude.bound: apparent (synodic) period within 0.25 percent of the reference sidereal period; semi-major axis (the amplitude) within 1 percent of the reference mean element; after the sidereal correction the period within 0.05 percent

c2.mass.claim: Kepler's third law on the fitted period and axis weighs Jupiter
c2.mass.bound: GM from each moon's truth marks within 1.0 percent of the planet's GM, 126,686,534 km^3/s^2, uncorrected for the Earth's motion; within 0.5 percent after the sidereal correction; the moon-to-moon scatter of the corrected values at most 0.3 percent

d1.coverage.claim: the stated uncertainties of the fit hold on an ensemble
d1.coverage.bound: over 200 seeded noise realisations (sigma 0.03 Jupiter radii, the designed epochs) the one-sigma interval holds the noise-free fit's period and amplitude between 58 and 78 percent of the time, for every moon

d2.massEnsemble.claim: the weighed mass is not claimed more precisely than it is known
d2.massEnsemble.bound: over the same 200 realisations the corrected GM of each moon lies within 3 stated sigmas of the planet's GM at least 95 percent of the time

e1.oracleFit.claim: the sinusoid fit is the least-squares fit
e1.oracleFit.bound: scipy curve_fit on the committed truth marks gives the same period and amplitude within 1e-5 relative

e2.inferenceCore.claim: the inference core's rv-keplerian fit of the same marks (a different code path) agrees on period and amplitude

f1.refusals.claim: the fit refuses what the cadence cannot support
f1.refusals.bound: fewer than eight marks, or a span shorter than one period, makes no period (refusal named in words); a moon whose best two candidates are within chi-square 9 is reported ambiguous with both periods

g1.frames.claim: the synthetic frames' centroids return the moons' positions
g1.frames.bound: centroid of each moon in a rendered frame within 0.15 pixel of the rendered position (0.02 Jupiter radii at this scale); the sequence digest is stable across runs
